thread:
mira: quick follow-up on the iterator/pagination retry shape we chatted about in the RFC thread. i sketched a tiny strawman for how python/ts/go could expose resume tokens + transport-level retries without leaking retry state into user code. want feedback before i turn it into a short RFC.
jon: +1 to getting something concrete. main worry: we don't want to force everybody to bubble idempotency keys into app code.
kai: curious about what "not leaking retry state" means here. can you paste the strawman?

mira: sure — idea is 3 primitives: 1) client.list_things(...) returns a lazy iterator/async iterable that yields items. 2) iterator exposes .resume_token() (opaque string) at any point. 3) transports can retry non-terminal failures internally; when a retry would *change* ordering or duplicate items we surface that via a transient error and caller can opt to resume from a token.

mira: python example:
```py
it = client.list_items(page_size=200)
for item in it:
    process(item)
    if should_snapshot():
        save_checkpoint(it.resume_token())
```

mira: ts/go similar shape: an AsyncIterable with `resume()` that accepts token. token is opaque base64 so we can change internals.
soph: i like keeping token opaque. question: how do we handle at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics? some customers rely on no-duplicates.
jon: runtime can't guarantee exactly-once across retries unless model/endpoint supports idempotent dedupe. so we should document "at-least-once unless you resume from a token" and provide helper for client-side dedupe using item IDs.
kai: what about exposing retry/backoff knobs? are we going to add retry policy objects to the surface? that tends to explode language surfaces.
mira: prefer minimal surface: global client retry config + per-call opt-outs. examples: `client = Client(retry=RetryConfig(...))` and `client.list(..., retry=None)` to disable. avoid per-iterator callbacks.
oliver: operationally we also want transport-level resume for streaming transports (grpc/long-poll/websocket). if we make token depend on transport state we need a migration plan when switching transport on the server side.
mira: exactly why token must be opaque and versioned. token payload can be `{v:2, t:..., cursor:...}` base64 encoded. server validates version and rejects if incompatible so client gets a clear error telling them to restart from beginning.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of transport-change-safe flag scheduled for next week :rocket:
soph: testing note — we should add deterministic resume tests in our integration harness: simulate mid-stream failure, resume with token, assert no gaps/acceptable duplicates. add both transports + short/long sequence lengths.
jon: also add an SDK migration guide: how to switch from old `page_token` loop patterns to this iterator + resume token flow. many users already snapshot page tokens.
kai: tiny pedantic point: want `resume_token()` to be cheap (no network). otherwise folks will snapshot aggressively and we defeat caching.
mira: agreed — resume_token must be purely local-iterator state.
oliver: for go surface I'd prefer an explicit `Resume(token string) (Iterator, error)` rather than a method on the iterator. easier for static typing.
mira: ok — make interfaces idiomatic per language but equivalent semantics. add examples in SDK repo and a crosslang test harness.
soph: rolling plan: 1) land transport + token encoding spec, 2) implement server-side accept/reject, 3) SDK prototypes in py/ts/go behind feature flag, 4) integrate tests, 5) doc + migration. sounds good?
mira: this is the plan i'm going to write up as a short RFC. thanks all — i'll ping when draft is up. :seedling:
jon: thanks, lgtm.

kai: nice, thanks — will review the RFC.

oliver: +1, also add a note about metrics (resume_count, resume_failures) so SRE can track customer impact.
